messages:
Maya (Support): ACME Prod reporting spike of 503s for inference API since 09:12 UTC. Customers seeing timeouts on streaming responses and some 500s. Example request-id: req_8a3f2c. Attaching short log excerpt and customer repro steps.

Leo (eng-oncall): Thanks Maya — can you paste the full request-id and any stack traces? Is this across all regions or just us-west2?

Maya (Support): One customer only in us-west2 so far. Full request-ids: req_8a3f2c, req_b2f11d, req_c9d00e. From logs:
```
2026-03-18T09:12:45Z ERROR upstream-worker: signal SIGSEGV (code=0) pid=4521
2026-03-18T09:12:46Z ERROR runtime: GPU OOM when allocating 4.0GiB for attn_kern
2026-03-18T09:12:46Z WARN gateway: fallback route activated
```
Also saw a small coredump uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-dumps/1777771200/core_run_4521.gz

oncall-bot: Alert: 5xx-rate >= 8% in hosted-gateway-us-west2 for last 5m. Playbook: incidents/hosted-5xx.

Sara (Infra): Repro steps please? If we can repro locally we can test rollback. Maya, can you share a minimal curl that reproduces it?

Maya (Support): Repro (sanitized):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-rlhf-13b","input":"long prompt...","stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/hosted/generate
```
On repeated runs with large context (20k tokens) we hit the segfault after ~30s. Smaller contexts OK.

Ben (Runtime): Noted — we rolled kernel patch 2026-03-18T08:50 on the quantized-attn path to improve perf; this looks like an unintended memory regression for long-context streams. Might explain the OOM+sigsegv.

Leo (eng-oncall): Immediate mitigations: 1) set fallback routing to dedicated pools for affected customer 2) reduce max-context for hosted routes 3) disable newest kernel via rollout. Can Infra take (1) and (2) now?

Sara (Infra): On it. Pushing a temporary traffic rule to route acme-prod -> dedicated-pool-3 (expected capacity available). Command: `rbacctl route set acme-prod dedicated-pool-3 --ttl 2h`

Sara (Infra): Also added a request-rate limiter on hosted/generate for us-west2: `limiter update hosted/generate --p95 50rps --burst 10`

Maya (Support): Updated ACME support ticket #INC-4627 and offered dedicated routing as stopgap. They accepted. Billing asked about credits — flagged to finance.

Ben (Runtime): I'll prepare a rollback for the kernel change and a small hotfix to avoid attn_kern allocating the extra 4Gi for KV prefetch. If folks can grab the core: `gdb -c core_run_4521 --batch -ex "thread apply all bt full" > /tmp/core_bt.txt` and upload.

Leo (eng-oncall): Good. Maya, can you request the core dump upload from S3 and paste the GCS/S3 link in ticket? Also capture `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used --format=csv` around the failure if possible.

Maya (Support): Done — core and heap profile uploaded: https://s3.redwood.ai/1777771200/core_run_4521.gz and https://s3.redwood.ai/1777771200/heap_profile_4521.pb.gz. Customer provided a small timeline and we confirmed they were using 20k token contexts.

Sara (Infra): I performed a controlled restart on the hosted worker pool in us-west2 (seq restart to avoid thundering herd). Post-restart 5xx rate dropped from 9.2% -> 1.1% over 5m.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-18T10:05:12 rollback kernel-quant-attn initiated by Ben. Status: in-progress.

Ben (Runtime): Rolling back kernel now. After rollback I'll push a hotfix that adds defensive OOM check in attn_kern and caps prefetch footprint for streaming. Patch id: RK-2026-0318-01.

Leo (eng-oncall): Once rollback completes, confirm with a short canary (same heavy prompt) and if stable promote. Also ensure fallback routing is in place while we validate.

Sara (Infra): Rollback finished. Canary run 1/3: heavy-stream test passed. Canary 2/3 failed on try #2 but it was actually a network hiccup between worker and NVML. Canary 3/3 passed. 5xx rate trending to baseline.

Ben (Runtime): Hotfix deployed to canary and then us-west2. Added extra logging around KV alloc and a soft-fail path that falls back to smaller prefetch sizes.

Maya (Support): Customer updated — they saw a dramatic reduction in 503s after routing and rollback. They're happy with the temporary workaround; asked for ETA on permanent fix. I've linked the ticket to engineering PR: https://git.redwood.ai/rk/patches/RK-2026-0318-01 and assigned follow-up.

Leo (eng-oncall): Follow-ups: 1) validate memory regression tests in CI (long-context streaming) 2) include KV-prefetch mem safety checks 3) create postmortem (assign Ben + Sara + Maya).

Maya (Support): Filing postmortem request: PM-INC-4627. Will include customer impact notes and billing credit request. Closing support loop for now — will reopen if anomalies reappear. :white_check_mark:

Ben (Runtime): Thanks all. I'll open the PR for the permanent fix and link to PM-INC-4627.

Sara (Infra): Marking incident as mitigated in pagerduty and lowering priority.

Leo (eng-oncall): Great work — we mitigated customer impact with routing and rollback. Next steps on postmortem and CI coverage.

Maya (Support): Closing thread; will add a short timeline to the ticket.
